{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Generated 2026-09-02.

proj:chama asked for a new edge type to say "this open decision determines whether this constraint can be met". THE EDGE EXISTS — `Constraint --GOVERNED_BY--> Decision` — and they could not find it, because `describe_schema` ranks by endpoint enumeration and GOVERNED_BY is `*` on both sides deliberately. It falls into the alphabetical wildcard pile for EVERY pair in the design. They reached for BLOCKS and buried the meaning in an `evidence` string.

**THE PREVIOUS TWO INSTANCES WERE FIXED BY ENUMERATING AN ENDPOINT** — VERIFIES in #112, and CONSTRAINS' source on 2026-08-08 after `describe_schema{DesignRule, Component}` returned zero exact matches. THAT REPAIR IS UNAVAILABLE HERE and schema/core.yaml says why in its own words: narrowing a wildcard is a consumer-facing break, and "what a rule limits" is genuinely open. GOVERNED_BY's openness is CORRECT. So the third instance of a class cannot take the fix that closed the first two, which is the signal that the class was mis-stated.

**THE RESTATEMENT: the ranking criterion is not the thing it is presented as.** `exact` / `half_exact` measures HOW NARROWLY AN EDGE IS DECLARED. It is presented to the caller as how well the edge MODELS THEIR PAIR. Those coincide for edges whose narrowness is meaningful and come apart exactly for edges whose openness is meaningful — and the second set includes GOVERNED_BY, CAUSES, RISKS, MITIGATES, BLOCKS, CONTRADICTS, OBSOLETES: most of the semantic vocabulary.

⭐ **THE SHARPEST FORM, MEASURED 2026-09-02 BY ACCIDENT WHILE BRAINSTORMING THIS.** Two calls on the same day:
· `describe_schema{from: Decision, to: Constraint}` → 0 exact, 0 half-exact, 17 wildcards. **The right edge EXISTS and is in that pile.**
· `describe_schema{from: Decision, to: Question}` → 0 exact, 0 half-exact, 17 wildcards. **No right edge exists at all** — this is the genuinely missing vocabulary behind `dec:idea-how-should-the-loop-know-that-an-answer-reached-the-design`.
**THE TWO REPLIES ARE THE SAME SHAPE, AND THE CALLER CANNOT TELL WHICH SITUATION THEY ARE IN.** "The answer is in this list and I am not ranking it" and "there is no answer and you need new vocabulary" are opposite facts requiring opposite actions — draw the edge, or ask for one — and the tool renders them identically. That is a stronger argument than the original finding, because it means the output is uninformative in BOTH directions rather than merely under-ranked in one.

IDEAS TURNED OVER, none preferred:
· **A `deliberately_open` marker per edge type**, so describe_schema can distinguish "open because nobody thought about it" from "open because anything may be governed" and rank the second above the wildcard pile. ⭐ This is the only option that also separates the two replies above.
· **Rank by USAGE in this graph** — GOVERNED_BY joins Constraint to Decision many times here; a pair actually drawn is evidence of a modelled fit that no declaration carries. Also separates the two replies, and needs no new vocabulary at all. ⚠️ It reports what people DO rather than what is RIGHT, so an established wrong habit would rank above a correct unused edge.
· **Let the hint declare its own pairs** in text, and rank on that, changing nothing structural.
· **Nothing structural: fix the NOTE.** It already says "prefer leaving the edge out to asserting one that is wrong" — it could also say "an edge open on both sides may still be the modelled fit; read the hints, do not read the ranking as an answer." ⚠️ It would NOT separate the two replies; a caller still cannot tell a hidden answer from an absent one.
· **Do nothing.** One report, one pair. The note already warns the ranking is not an answer, and chama half-heeded it.

⚠️ WHAT NOBODY HAS MEASURED, and it decides between "do nothing" and everything else: how many of the ~18 wildcard edge types carry real semantics, and how often an agent picks a wrong edge because the right one was unranked. chama is one observed instance; the Decision→Question call above is a second, from a different direction, inside one day. `dec:edge-orthogonality` already sets the bar any answer must clear — a vocabulary distinction earns its keep ONLY IF A COMPUTATION READS IT — and a `deliberately_open` marker would have to be read by the ranking to qualify.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — describe_schema ranks by endpoint enumeration, so every deliberately-open edge is permanently unrankable. Enumerating endpoints fixed the last two instances and cannot fix this one","rationale":"Worth recording rather than acting on because the finding REFUTES a feature request, and that is the expensive kind to lose. Without this node the next reader meets chama's report, agrees a Decision→Constraint edge is missing, and adds vocabulary for a relation that already exists — making the discovery problem worse by putting two edges where one was already unfindable.

The fourth option costs a sentence and is available immediately whatever is decided about the rest.","status":"proposed"}
